Vancouver, BC – October 23, 2026 - TheNewswire – Uranium One  Mining Corp. ("Uranium One" or the "Company") (UUU: CSE | UUUFF: OTCID | SL51: Frankfurt) is pleased to announce that it has engaged Adrian Huerta Ruiz as a Technical Advisor focused on the Company’s uranium exploration interests in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin.
About Huerta Ruiz, CPG

Mr. Huerta Ruiz is an experienced exploration geologist and Certified Professional Geologist (CPG) with the American Institute of Professional Geologists (AIPG), bringing more than 14 years of technical and operational experience in mineral exploration and mining.

Based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Mr. Huerta Ruiz has direct experience working on uranium exploration projects in the Athabasca Basin, including geological core logging and sampling of sandstone- and basement-hosted uranium systems. His expertise encompasses exploration program management, drill planning, geological mapping, geological interpretation, and quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) procedures.

In his role as Technical Advisor to Uranium One Mining Corp., Mr. Huerta Ruiz is expected to provide technical guidance and support the evaluation, planning and prioritization of exploration activities across the Company's Athabasca Basin uranium portfolio, including preparations for its upcoming field exploration season.

“We are pleased to have Adrian joining the Uranium One team,” said Larry Segerstrom, Director and P.Geo. “His experience adds to our technical strength as the Company prepares for its maiden exploration season in the Athabasca Basin. We look forward to his input as we evaluate our properties and set priorities for fieldwork.”
Uranium One’s Athabasca Basin Portfolio

The Company’s portfolio comprises three highly prospective uranium projects in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin, which is widely recognized as the world’s premier jurisdiction for high-grade uranium deposits. These are the Pasfield Lake, Quark, and Nucleon projects.
Pasfield Lake Project, Athabasca Basin

The Pasfield Lake Project is Uranium One’s flagship Canadian uranium exploration asset, encompassing approximately 4,400 hectares in Saskatchewan’s eastern Athabasca Basin. Strategically located approximately 60 kilometres northwest of Cameco’s Cigar Lake Mine, the project occupies a highly prospective geological setting where favourable basement rocks, major regional fault systems, and historical exploration results combine to create an exceptional exploration opportunity.
Click Image To View Full Size

Historical work completed by previous operators has generated an extensive technical database, including airborne geophysical surveys, Audio Magnetotelluric (AMT) surveys, gravity surveys, geochemistry, and diamond drilling. This comprehensive dataset provides Uranium One with a strong foundation to apply modern exploration techniques and advanced targeting methods in the search for a significant uranium discovery.
Quark Uranium Claim Group – Athabasca Basin

The Quark Project consists of a large, contiguous land package of approximately 28,746 hectares (71,030 acres), situated within the highly productive Western Wollaston Domain and Wollaston–Mudjatik Transition Zone—host to the majority of Canada’s past and present uranium mines.
Click Image To View Full Size

Positioned adjacent to and along trend with major industry operators including Orano Canada and Fission Uranium, Quark benefits from proximity to established infrastructure, proven mineralization corridors, and active exploration success.
Nucleon Claim Group
The Nucleon Uranium Project consists of seven exploration-stage mineral claims totaling approximately 23,424.90 hectares located in northern Saskatchewan, Canada, within the Athabasca Basin.
The project is organized into four prospective exploration areas situated along key uranium discovery corridors in the Basin.

The Athabasca Basin hosts some of the highest-grade uranium deposits in the world and accounts for a significant portion of global uranium supply, making it one of the most important uranium-producing regions internationally.
The Nucleon claims are positioned within an active uranium exploration district surrounded by major discoveries and development projects, including those operated by:
NexGen Energy (Arrow deposit)
Fission Uranium (Patterson Lake South deposit)
Denison Mines
Cameco
This strategic location places the project within a highly prospective geological corridor known for multiple major uranium discoveries.
Mineralization on nearby properties or at nearby mines is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on Uranium One’s properties.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Lawrence Segerstrom, a consulting geologist who is a “Qualified Person” as such term is defined under National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”).
The QP reviewed the technical content, including the figures, historical data summaries, and adjacent property information, and confirms that the data have been accurately summarized where used.
Restricted Stock Units

The Company announces that it has granted an aggregate of 3,400,000 restricted share units (“RSUs”) to certain officers, directors and consultants of the Company pursuant to its restricted share unit plan (the “RSU Plan”). The RSUs have a term of one year from the date of grant and are subject to the terms and conditions of the RSU Plan and applicable policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange (the “CSE”).
About Uranium One Mining Corp.

Uranium One Mining Corp. is a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on the acquisition, exploration, and development of uranium projects and select battery metals assets. The Company is advancing a diversified portfolio of high-potential projects in Canada, Paraguay and Argentina, with a strategic focus on assets positioned to benefit from the increasing global demand for nuclear energy and secure energy supply chains.

The Company’s projects include the Quark Uranium Project, the Yuty Prometeo Uranium Project, and the Nucleon Uranium Project, each of which offers significant exploration upside and potential for resource expansion.

Uranium One Mining Corp. is committed to responsible exploration practices, disciplined capital allocation, and the creation of long-term shareholder value through the systematic advancement of its project portfolio.
